latin: Rectius est ut AMEN tipheret dicat et regnum, ut per uiam numeri ostenditur, quam quod dicat regnum tantum, ut quidam uolunt.
translation: It is more correct to say that AMEN denotes both Tiferet and kingdom, as the way of number shows, than to say, with some, that it denotes kingdom alone.
translation_note: Farmer's note reads this as a planned gematria proof of the interconvertibility of AMEN, Tiferet (the sixth sefirah) and kingdom (the tenth); since Pico elsewhere ties Tiferet, 'the great Adam', to Christ, the equation would carry a Christological weight (farmer1998:27858).
